newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: KEPPEL HITS NEW LOW, FLAT EARNINGS SEEN.
newsitem.headline: KEPPEL HITS NEW LOW, FLAT EARNINGS SEEN.

text.p: Shares in diversified maritime group Keppel Corp sank to a new year low of Singapore $5.60 on Thursday ahead of its six-months earnings report, dealers said.
"It's a combination of market sentiment and the fact that some analysts have pared down its interim earnings," said a dealer with a local institution.
At 0815 GMT, the shares had recovered to S$5.85 in active trade of over 3.6 million shares.
Keppel is expected to announce its profits for six months ended June 1997 towards the end of August.
The group's profit for the first half of 1997 was expected to be flat at S$95 million to S$100 million, analysts said.
For 1997, while the group's ship repair business continued to struggle, analysts said earnings could be further pressured by its shipbuilding unit, Keppel FELS Ltd.
"We are expecting a sharp fall from FELS because they don't have any contracts to book this year, unlike last year. All the completions will be booked only in 1998," said one analyst.
Analysts have also pared down the group's 1997 income from from treasury and investments.
However, some are calling investors with a medium term outlook to buy or accumulate the stock.

"I think the company is going to reverse its negative earnings trend seen the last few years," said Sim Chey Hoon, investment analyst at Merrill Lynch, who was calling an accumulate on the stock at current levels up to low $6.
Continued growth generators remain the group's banking unit Keppel Bank, property arm Keppel Land and telecommunications business through Keppel Telecom.
